newsitem.title: FINLAND: SALOMON SEES FALLING PAPER PRICES IN 1997 - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: SALOMON SEES FALLING PAPER PRICES IN 1997 - PAPER.

text.p: U.S. investment bank Salomon Brothers expects paper prices to fall significantly in 1997, business daily Kauppalehti reported Tuesday.
Salomon expects newsprint prices to fall 15 percent in 1997 after an 11 percent rise in 1996, the paper said.

According to Salomon, prices of sc-paper (super calendered) would fall about 14 percent in 1997 after a four percent drop this year, and prices of lwc-paper (light weight coated) would fall seven percent after a nine percent fall in 1996, it said.
Lower paper prices in Europe would follow bigger imports from Canada and capacity increases in 1997 and 1998, Kauppalehti quoted Salomon Brothers as saying.
Also, growth in demand would remain below the long-term average, it said.
The investment bank forecast pulp prices to be at about $575 per tonne in 1997 after falling to $573 from $883 in 1996, the paper said.
